transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

Um... well, I came in because... I guess my mind just keeps going blank? It's a little embarrassing to admit, and it's probably just me being a little scattered lately, but it happens at the worst times. Like, I work as a flagger, and I'll just look at the road-closure forms, or even just be holding my stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I... I just cannot remember the steps. Things I've done perfectly for years, and it's just gone. 

I'm sorry, does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it the right way for you.
When your mind goes blank like that, do you feel very anxious right then?

Um... no, not really anxious, I don't think. I mean, I hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression, I'm not panicking or anything like that. It's more just... empty? Like the thoughts just stop. 

I know it sounds silly, and I'm probably making a bigger deal out of it than it is. I just stand there for a minute and try to catch up. Does that help? I want to make sure I'm answering your question the way you need me to.
When this happens, do you later have a gap in your memory for what happened during that moment?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I remember standing there, and I remember feeling confused. It's not like I black out or anything scary like that, I promise. I just... I just lose my train of thought. 

I'm still fully aware of where I am and everything. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details so you can do your job. Am I explaining that okay?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Um... well, I guess maybe a little bit? I really don't want to sound ungrateful or like I'm just complaining, because I know I have a lot to be thankful for and people have it way worse. 

But... um... lately, most mornings I wake up with this... this really heavy, hollow sadness right in my chest. It kind of feels like the day is already ruined before I even put my feet on the floor. I always try my best to push past it and put on a brave face, I promise. 

I hope it's okay that I'm admitting that? I feel a little bad sounding so negative to you, but I want to make sure I'm being honest so I'm giving you the right information. Is that what you meant?
Have you been feeling that heavy sadness nearly every day?

Um... yes, I think so. Almost every day, I'd say. I really try not to let it get to me, I really do. But yeah, it's pretty much every morning that I wake up with that... that heavy feeling. 

I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm answering you right. I don't want to sound like a broken record or like I'm whining. I know I should just be able to shake it off and get ready for work, you know? But it's just... it's there almost every day. Does that make sense? I hope I'm being helpful.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Um, well... I guess I've been having a little bit of a hard time with that, yeah. I really hate to admit it because I try so hard to do a good job at work. But... um... honestly, that's kind of why I came in to see you. 

My mind just keeps going blank at the worst times. Like, I'll be at work—I'm a crossing guard and flagger—and I'll look at the road-closure forms or even just my stop-slow paddle, and suddenly... I just cannot remember the steps. And I've done this for years! It's so embarrassing. 

I always try to cover it up so nobody notices, I promise I'm not putting anyone in danger. I just... I don't want my boss to think I'm incompetent, you know? Is it normal to have trouble focusing like that? I hope I'm explaining it right, I just want to make sure you have all the pieces.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I still try to keep up with the things I usually do. I really make an effort to stay positive and engaged, I promise. 

I guess I haven't been doing as much lately, but I think that's just because I've been so tired, you know? Not because I don't like those things anymore. I still want to enjoy them. I always try to force myself to get out and do things so I'm not just sitting around moping. 

I hope that's a good thing? I really don't want to seem like I'm just giving up on everything. Does that answer your question okay?
Have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty lately?

Um... well, I really try not to let myself think that way, because I know I should be grateful for what I have. But... yes, I guess I have been feeling a lot of guilt lately. I'm sorry to even say it, I know I shouldn't be so hard on myself.

It's just... I keep replaying every little thing I feel like I've failed at. Like with my friend, or the choir, or even my own family. I just keep thinking about all the things I didn't do right, or the times I wasn't there for them enough. And... um... sometimes I just feel like I'm a completely useless person. Like I deserve whatever punishment is coming my way because I've let everyone down. 

I know that sounds terrible, and I really try to push those thoughts away, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around throwing a pity party. Is it normal to feel that guilty over little things? I hope I'm not overreacting.
Have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself?

Um... oh, that's a really hard question. I... I really don't want to worry you, and I promise I'm not trying to be dramatic or anything. I know I should be stronger than this. 

But... um... honestly, I've just been so exhausted lately. I feel terrible even admitting it, but sometimes I just... I don't have the energy to fight off those thoughts anymore. The ones that say it might just be easier if I went to sleep and... and didn't wake up. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds awful. I really try to keep it to myself because I don't want to be a burden, but I guess I've started saying it out loud without meaning to, and... it's really scaring my family. I hate that I'm putting them through that, I really do. I want to be better for them. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making things sound worse than they are, I just want to make sure I'm answering you honestly so you can help me.
Have you noticed a change in your sleep lately?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I think I'm sleeping okay? I really try to keep a good schedule, you know, so I'm rested for work and everything. 

I guess maybe I've been a little tired, but honestly, I think my sleep is mostly fine. I always make sure to go to bed at a reasonable hour, I promise. I don't want to complain about something as small as sleep when there are so many other things going on. 

Does that sound right? I hope I'm giving you the right information. I just don't think there's been any big change there.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite lately?

Um... well, I really do try to eat properly, I promise. I know I need to keep my strength up for work. I don't want you to think I'm purposely starving myself or anything like that... 

It's just... I guess food has kind of stopped meaning much to me lately? I'll be out there working and I just... I end up skipping meals without even noticing. I honestly didn't think it was a big deal until my flagger pants started getting really loose on me. And... um... my family has started asking why I look so drawn. I feel terrible making them worry about me like that. I know I should be taking better care of myself. 

I'll definitely try harder to eat, I really will. Is it normal to just lose interest in food when you're feeling like this? I hope I'm not doing something wrong.
Have you been moving or speaking noticeably slower than usual lately?

Um... well, I really try my best to keep up with everything, I promise I do. I don't want to be a bother or make anyone wait on me. 

But... I guess my family has been pointing out that I'm taking a lot longer to get ready in the mornings? Like, it just takes me so much effort to bathe and get dressed and actually make it to the door. They... they told me I look like I'm moving underwater. I feel so bad that they have to wait for me. I really am trying to go faster. 

And then... sometimes it's the opposite? Like, I'll get so worked up that I can't settle down at all, and I just end up pacing the hallway and wringing my hands. I know it must be so annoying for them to watch. I'm really trying to act more normal, I swear. 

Is it okay that I'm having trouble with both? I hope I'm explaining this right for you.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um... well, I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. I've been trying so hard to just push through it and do my job and be there for my family. I don't want you to think I'm just giving up or anything. 

But I guess... if I really think about it... it's been a while. Maybe about a year and eight months? It all sort of started after my closest friend passed away. I know people lose friends all the time and they manage to cope just fine, and I really should be doing better by now. I'm so sorry, I know I shouldn't still be letting it affect me this much. 

I'm trying my best to get back to normal, I promise. Does that... does that timeline make sense to you? I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with all this.
Do you still feel intense longing or yearning for the friend who died?

Um... well, no, not really. I mean, I miss her, of course I do. She was a wonderful person. But I really try not to dwell on it too much, I promise. I know it's not healthy to just sit around yearning for someone who's gone. 

I really try to focus on the good memories and keep moving forward, like I know she'd want me to. I don't want you to think I'm just wallowing in the past or refusing to accept what happened. I've been trying so hard to be strong about it. 

I mean, there are moments where it hits me, but... but I don't feel that intense longing you mentioned. Is that... is that the right way I should be handling it? I hope I'm grieving the right way.
Have you had any recent head injury?

Um... no, no head injuries. I'm always really careful, especially with my job. Being out there on the road, directing traffic, you know, I always make sure to wear my helmet if I'm biking, and I'm always looking out for my safety and everyone else's. I really try to be responsible about that kind of thing. 

So, no, nothing like that. I haven't hit my head or been in any accidents or anything. I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I'm glad I don't have to add that to the list of things you have to worry about with me.
Outside of those blank moments at work, have you been forgetting important things more often than usual?

Um... well, I really hope I'm not making a big deal out of nothing. I mean, everyone forgets things sometimes, right? I don't want you to think I'm losing my mind or that I can't do my job. I really try to stay on top of everything.

But... I guess that's actually kind of why I came in. It's just... my mind keeps going blank at the absolute worst times. Like, I'll be looking at the road-closure forms, or holding my stop-slow paddle, and suddenly... I just can't remember the steps. And I've been doing this for years! It's so embarrassing. 

I really try to cover it up so no one notices, and I always figure it out eventually, I promise. I'm not putting anyone in danger. It's just... it's been scaring me a little bit, to be honest. Is that... is it normal to have moments like that when you're under a lot of stress? I really hope I'm not failing at my job.
When you're not at work, do you ever forget familiar steps for everyday tasks you've done for years?

Um... no, not really. I mean, at home, I'm pretty good about keeping things together. I don't want you to think I'm completely falling apart or anything. I can still cook and clean and take care of myself just fine, I promise. 

I really try to keep a good routine going when I'm not at work, you know? It helps keep me grounded. So, no, I haven't been forgetting how to do my laundry or make coffee or anything like that. It's just... it just seems to happen when I'm out there on the road, with all the noise and the cars. 

I hope that makes sense? Like, I'm still capable of doing all my normal, everyday things. I'm trying really hard to make sure everything stays normal at home, at least. That's a good sign, isn't it?
When you're out on the road and your mind goes blank, do you suddenly feel like you're reliving something upsetting?

Um... no, no, nothing like that. I really don't want you to think I'm having, like, flashbacks or anything scary like that. I promise it's not like that at all. 

It's just... a blankness. Like a pause button gets hit, you know? I'm not trapped in some terrible memory or anything. I'm just standing there, and for a second, I just lose my train of thought. 

I really try to keep a positive mindset when I'm out there, and I don't have any, um, traumatic things that I'm reliving. I hope that's reassuring? I mean, it's just a little forgetfulness, not... not anything really serious like that. I'm doing okay mentally in that regard, I promise.
Do you actually believe you deserve to be punished for having let people down?

Um... well... I know I probably shouldn't think this way, and I don't want to sound dramatic or anything. I try really hard to be a good person, I do. But... 

It's just... lately, I can't stop replaying all these things in my head. Like, every little thing I failed to do. For my friend, for the choir I used to be in, and... and for my own family. I just keep thinking about how much I've let everyone down. 

I don't want you to think I'm wallowing in it, I really try to push it away! But sometimes I just feel so... useless. Like I'm just a burden, and... and if something bad happens to me, if some kind of punishment is coming... I probably deserve it. 

I know that's a terrible thing to say, and I'm sorry. I really don't want to be a downer. I'm trying to work on it, I promise. Is it... is it normal to feel that guilty when you've made mistakes? I just want to make sure I'm not saying the wrong thing.
